prompt: Which two roles should never be held by the same person, by the lesson?
hint: The updates stop when it is hardest.

choices.text: Commander and communications, since both talk to leadership
choices.why: Not the combination named.

choices.text: Commander and scribe
choices.why: Possible in a small incident.

choices.text: Operations and communications
choices.why: Right: the updates stop exactly when people most want them.

choices.text: Scribe and operations lead in a long incident
choices.why: Not ideal, and not the one the lesson singles out.

prompt: From 19:09 to 19:41, how many minutes did checkout fail?
Why did Bruna open one dedicated incident channel?

choices.text: So everything about it lives in one place
choices.why: Right: a complete timeline, no four threads, and nobody needs to ask where.

choices.text: To keep leadership out of the technical discussion
choices.why: Leadership gets its own updates; the channel is open.

choices.text: Because the engineering channel was down too
choices.why: It was not.

choices.text: Company policy requires a channel per incident for audit purposes
choices.why: Not the reason given.

prompt: Put the status page labels in order.

choices.text: What is being done
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: The impact, in the reader's terms
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: The most likely cause, even if unconfirmed
choices.why: A guess published has to be corrected publicly.

choices.text: When the next update will come
choices.why: Yes: and it comes when it said.

prompt: At 19:31 Lucas suspects the backfill. Why does Lívia not write "we think a batch job"?

choices.text: Lucas asked her not to
choices.why: Nothing says so.

choices.text: Customers do not care about causes during an incident
choices.why: They care; the risk is giving a wrong one.

choices.text: A wrong cause, once published, is corrected in public
choices.why: Right: she waited for the confirmation at 19:38.

choices.text: Because naming a batch job blames the team that runs it
choices.why: "A background job" names no one; the issue is that it was unconfirmed.

prompt: How many minutes after checkout began failing did the first public update go out?

choices.text: The first status page update
choices.why: Useful, and not the one named.

choices.text: The update to leadership saying no action was needed
choices.why: Important for leadership, not the most useful.

choices.text: A ready sentence for support to say to customers
choices.why: Right: something true to say, and permission to say it.

choices.text: The explanation of connection pools sent to support

prompt: Why does the summary say "cause, as far as we know"?

choices.text: To avoid legal liability if a customer complains later about the outage
choices.why: The customer letter takes responsibility plainly.

choices.text: It is a phrase required by the template
choices.why: The lesson argues for it, not from a template.

choices.text: Because nobody knew the cause on Saturday morning
choices.why: The immediate cause was known; the review finds the rest.

choices.text: The review, still to come, looks for more than one cause
choices.why: Right: it is accuracy, not hedging.

prompt: What does the customer letter contain? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: A promise that it can never happen again
choices.why: Nobody can keep that promise.

choices.text: What it means for them, a credit included
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: An apology that takes responsibility
choices.why: Yes: the cause was Marola's own system.

choices.text: What happened, in their terms
choices.why: Yes.

prompt: Two engineers read "since 22:10" in different time zones. What rule did Marola adopt?

choices.text: Times are left out of incident messages
choices.why: Times are essential; the zone was missing.

choices.text: All times are written in UTC from now on
choices.why: A choice some teams make; Marola states the zone instead.

choices.text: Only the scribe writes times, to keep them consistent
choices.why: Everybody writes times; the rule is the zone.

choices.text: Every time carries its zone, or the template states it once
choices.why: Right: "all times Recife (UTC−3)" at the top.

prompt: Which is the lesson's replacement for "the database died"?

choices.text: "Back to normal"
choices.why: Says nothing about what happened.

choices.text: "Paulo's job killed the database"
choices.why: Blame and alarm.

choices.text: "It stopped accepting connections; no data was lost"
choices.why: Right: the effect, and what did not happen.

choices.text: "A minor database issue"
choices.why: Understates, and is read as hiding.

prompt: Twenty minutes into an incident, nothing new is known and the next update is due. What should the communications lead post?

choices.text: Impact unchanged, still working, next update at a stated time
choices.why: Right: the update comes when it said, even if nothing changed.

choices.text: Nothing, until there is something new
choices.why: Silence is read as nobody working, or worse than said.

choices.text: An estimate of fifteen minutes to the fix, to reassure people
choices.why: A promise she cannot keep.

choices.text: The most likely cause, to show progress
choices.why: An unconfirmed cause published must be corrected publicly.
